Document type: adjuster_file. Page 1 of 2.

<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1059
Claimant:
Kristina Brown
Adjuster:
Valerie Rodriguez
9-3-23
The claimant reported a low-speed head-on collision and stated that the vehicle was struck while travelling in a single
lane. The claimant is not represented by counsel and was asked to provide a written account.
9-16-23
Police attendance is confrimed and the responding officer recorded the claimant as the driver of the vehicle at the
scene. The report is on file.
10-24-23
Witness statements were obtained from two bystanders who describe the impact exactly as the claimant did. Both
witnesses are willing to be contacted again if needed.
10-29-23
Photographs of the vehicle show front-end damage that is consistent with the reported impact. The pattern and
location of the damage line up with a head-on contact.
11-19-23
The other driver's account matches the claimant's description of how the collision occurred. No conflict has been
identified between the two statements.
12-8-23
The claimant described the same sequence of events in the first call, the recorded statement and the follow-up
interview. Details were consistent throughout.
12-19-23
The claimant reports neck and back strain and states that symptoms began shortly after the collision. The reported
injuries are the type typically associated with a collision of this force.
1-20-24
Medical records show the claimant attended treatment at a usual pace, with care tapering as symptoms improved. No
unusual gaps or escalations appear in the file.
1-23-24
Prior records were checked and no earlier injury to the neck or back has been found. The claimant also confirmed no
previous complaints in that area.
2-12-24
Vehicle history was reviewed and no earlier damage to the vehicle has been identified. Nothing in the records
suggests the damage predates the policy period.
2-22-24
The driver is listed as a named driver on the policy, and the coverage was in force on the date of loss. Nothing has
been found to question the policy status.
4-6-24
Based on the photos, wintess accounts, police report and medical file, the claim is progressing as a standard
low-speed collision with a routine injury course. File is being prepared for settlement review.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
